record.what_it_does: Shared inbox and customer communication platform for support teams, unifying email, chat, SMS and more.
record.auth_notes: OAuth2 authorization code grant only. Token exchange uses Basic auth with client ID and secret. Access tokens last 60 minutes, and refresh tokens last 6 months. API calls use Bearer tokens. Front also has company-level API tokens, which are not confirmed on a fetched page. Authorizing users of OAuth apps must be admins. The MCP server is the exception, because it uses user-scoped tokens.
record.access_notes: The developer portal says a developer account gives a free developer environment. OAuth is required for public integrations unless Front grants an exception. No app-review step is described on the OAuth page, but listing in the Front App Store may involve Front's own review, which I did not confirm. I could not verify which Front plans allow API or token access.
record.api_breadth_notes: The Core API covers conversations, messages, contacts, inboxes, teammates, tags, comments, drafts, channels, rules and more. The Channel API is separate. I did not count operations.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp. It uses OAuth, is listed in Claude's connector directory, and is described as GA-stable as of August 2026 (it began as a beta in April 2026). Docs: https://dev.frontapp.com/docs/mcp-server
record.blocker_notes: Minor caveats: OAuth authorizers must be admins, and the official MCP server already exists. The exact plan requirements for API access were not confirmed.

evidence.quote: End users authorizing OAuth apps must be admins.
OAuth is required for public integrations available to all Front customers, unless Front grants an exception.
Application webhooks retry failed deliveries, so a transient failure on your side does not mean a lost event.
Front's MCP server (mcp.frontapp.com/mcp) lets AI agents act on Front conversation data using a single OAuth-authenticated endpoint.
Core API spec is viewable on GitHub (frontapp/front-api-specs)

record.needs_human: Several points rest on search-result summaries, not on pages I opened. These are the free developer environment (I did not open the developer portal homepage), the OpenAPI repo (frontapp/front-api-specs), and the MCP details. Please check three things: (1) which Front plans allow API token and OAuth app creation, (2) whether the free dev environment is a true sandbox or a time-limited trial, and (3) whether the public App Store listing needs Front's approval. The page for API tokens returned a 404.
